newsitem.title: USA: Battered US spot prods take another hit after APIs.
newsitem.headline: Battered US spot prods take another hit after APIs.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products prices were thrashed in another NYMEX selloff late Tuesday, with the damage compounded by further losses in after-hours ACCESS trade spurred by bearish API inventory data.
Heating oil and gasoline were down about 0.70 cent a gallon in ACCESS activity after tumbling 2.51 cents and 2.02 cents, respectively, in the earlier NYMEX session.
Traders predicted the API's estimate of a six million barrel build in total U.S. gasoline stocks for the week ending Dec 6 would keep downard pressure on.
Cash buyers were scarce in both the Gulf Coast and New York Harbor all day, players said, a repeat of their reluctance Monday to buy barrels in a downswing market.
"The (API) gasoline build is huge. The No. 2 (heating oil) build is huge. These aren't good numbers -- the market is going to move lower," one Gulf Coast products trader said of the API estimates.
"The APIs should bury the gasoline market," one Gulf gasoline trader said. "It's been nothing but sellers for the last four days and now this! It won't be pretty," he said.
